verdicts.explanation: Section 2.2 gives 3.26 mS cm-1 at 35 ℃ for Li6PS5Cl as the experimental value, compared against the AIMD prediction of 3.23. The Ea of 0.25 eV and the 530 °C / 10 h anneal from Methods also match.
Section 2.2 reports 2.8 mS cm-1 at 35 ℃ for Li6.25PS4O1.25Cl0.75 as measured, with Ea = 0.33 eV, and the anneal conditions are from Methods.

The paper states the Li6.25PS4O1.25Cl0.75 conductivity at -20 ℃ is 1.49 mS cm-1, measured experimentally, and the conclusion repeats it. No activation energy is given for this value, so null is correct.

The sentence 'comparable with that of the pristine Li6PS5Cl sulfide (2.32 mS cm-1)' gives 2.32 mS cm-1 for pristine Li6PS5Cl at -20 ℃, which is the temperature of the preceding sentence. The material, value and origin are correct.

Section 2.3 reports 1.5 mS cm-1 at room temperature for the post-annealed Li6.25PS4O1.25Cl0.75 after humid-air exposure, measured in this work. Null for the temperature number and for the sintering fields is consistent with the paper.

The Introduction attributes the 12 mS cm-1 room-temperature conductivity of Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 to an earlier report ([51]), so literature_cited is the correct origin and the record's fields are otherwise consistent.
